subject: Media Literacy
title: Bias in Science Reporting
description: A quick win: understand Bias in Science Reporting.

hook.text: A headline reads 'Coffee Causes Cancer.' The study found a tiny correlation in rats given extreme doses.

buildup.text: Science reporting suffers from bias toward dramatic findings, oversimplification, and ignoring uncertainty.

discovery.text: Journalists often report single studies as breakthroughs while ignoring the broader body of evidence.

twist.text: Preliminary findings get headlines. Replication failures and corrections rarely make the news.

climax.text: Reading science news critically means checking the study size, source, funding, and whether experts agree.

punchline.text: One study isn't proof. A headline about one study is even less.

quiz.question: What is a common bias in science reporting?
options: Presenting single studies as breakthroughs while ignoring broader evidence
